item.title: SCP-5290:
item.content:encoded:
A few nitpicks to your nitpicks

Councilmember as a single word exists and is used correctly.

Transparent objects can be colored? Like, you know, colored glass, plastics and whatnot. Color doesn't make an object inherently not transparent. It could've been a transparent blue prism, for example

Sometimes redactions and expunged data is used to get rid of unimportant information that doesn't really matter to the story, like the amount of dollars earned by use of an anomaly.

item.title: SCP-3790-J:
item.content:encoded: I initially downvoted because I didn't laugh once, but I did appreciate all the cute references left and right and how charmingly crafted it all was. Humor is subjective, so I'll acknowledge quality when I see it, even if it doesn't tickle me personally. Despite me acknowledging the quality, I'm still disappointingly un-tickled, so, No-vote. My apologies.

item.title: SCP-682: Re: why are they trying to kill it
item.content:encoded:
One modern theory rooted in a couple different branches of site lore is that there's some sort of stealthy compulsion effect at work, and/or that there's a deeper reason that 682 has to suffer endlessly.

There's also the fact that it escapes regularly and kills a bunch of people even if they don't try to kill it, so it's worth a shot on the off chance that something works.

item.title: SCP-3030:
item.content:encoded:
Too many words. That surmises the sticking issue of the article.

Both containment and description are unnecessary lengthy, usually to throw unnecessary badassery, redundant information or some flourish. Not all, but most references to O5s and MTFs can be removed here.

After trimming down the text, add paragraphs on the incident description to make it more readable and explain if the Central Plaza is within the five -2s or in the non-affected sectors.

Otherwise this was a very good SCP. To me it is more interesting than 2000 as a Thaumiel-ish thing.

item.title: SCP-4504:
item.content:encoded:
Note: The last thing I did before reading this article was read SCP-5031, which is basically its exact opposite.

My god. He was a good guy. He could have been fine, an asset even. But they made him an object, treated him worse than an animal, and what they got was a monster. God damn them all to hell.

The most chilling part of this is the stellar use of clinical tone to cover up reasonable, unscientific reactions to the fucked-up shit taking place in the story. And it ends in the absolute fucking perfect spot. God damn. God damn. +1

item.title: SCP-5031:
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5031 has said its first word: "Salt".

We are all immensely proud.

Sir, I protest, this is illegal. ;_;

This is somehow both the most heartwarming shit and the most scathing indictment of 'classic' Foundation I have ever seen. +1 isn't enough reward for this article.

Also, I highly approve of the use of Ben Folds to pacify murder monsters.
